UPSTREAM: drm/amd/display: Explicitly call ->reset for each object We need to avoid calling reset after detection because the next commit adds freesync properties on the atomic_state which are set during detection. Calling reset after this clears them. The easiest way to accomplish this right now is to call ->reset on the connector right after creation but before detection. To stay consistent call ->reset on every other object as well after creation. v2: Provide better reason for this change in commit msg. BUG=b:65489307 TEST=boot Kahlee, run graphics_SanAngeles Signed-off-by: Harry Wentland <harry.wentland@amd.com> Reviewed-by: Roman Li <Roman.Li@amd.com> Acked-by: Harry Wentland <harry.wentland@amd.com> Reviewed-by: Andrey Grodzovsky <andrey.grodzovsky@amd.com> Signed-off-by: Alex Deucher <alexander.deucher@amd.com> (cherry picked from commit 96719c5439b4d75bfd6b3c5cb24f1a8e537125bb) Signed-off-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@chromium.org> Change-Id: I3b7c7ec6df40df5e5495269a92964dd0ee78c1a2 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/847244 Commit-Ready: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Tested-by: Dominik Behr <dbehr@google.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: drm/amd/display: small cleanup in destruct() Static analysis tools get annoyed that we don't indent this if statement. Actually, the if statement isn't required because kfree() can handle NULL pointers just fine. The DCE110STRENC_FROM_STRENC() macro is a wrapper around container_of() but it's basically a no-op or a cast. Anyway, it's not really appropriate here so it should be removed as well. UPSTREAM: drm/amd/display: Fix warnings on S3 resume This is a followup to the following revert: Rex Zhu Revert "drm/amd/display: Match actual state during S3 resume." Three things needed to be addressed: 1. Potential memory leak on dc_state creation in atomic_check during s3 resume 2. Warnings are now seen in dmesg during S3 resume 3. Since dc_state is now created in atomic_check, what the reverted patch was addressing needs to be reevaluated. This change addresses the above: 1. Since the suspend procedure calls drm_atomic_state_clear, our hook for releasing the dc_state is called. This frees it before atomic_check creates it during resume. The leak does not occur. 2. The dc_crtc/plane_state references kept by the atomic states need to be released before calling atomic_check, which warns if they are non-null. This is because atomic_check is responsible for creating the dc_*_states. This is a special case for S3 resume, since the atomic state duplication that occurs during suspend also copies a reference to the dc_*_states. 3. See 2. comments are also updated to reflect this. shill: prefer leaky base::LazyInstance when appropriate For base::LazyInstance objects that don't really require any actual cleanup (e.g. releasing system resources) when the process terminates, there is no benefit in destructing them through base::ExitManager. This CL makes these LazyInstance objects in shill as leaky. Also note that Leaky base::LazyInstance objects could be turned into simple function-scoped statics as function-scoped static initializers are thread-safe (unless being disabled via a compiler option) in C++11. But base::LazyInstance<T>::Leaky annotates the underlying leaky object to suppress warnings from LeakSanitizer. So instead of switching the code to use function-scoped statics, we continue to use base::LazyInstance<T>::Leaky. BUG=None TEST=Run unit tests.
